paper.title: Preferenced Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies for Dynamic Bipedal Loco-Manipulation
paper.source_version: arXiv v3, revised 2025-10-08; cross-checked against the IROS 2025 publisher record and official project/code

decision_relevance.why_admitted: The paper gives a concrete closed-loop hybrid-automaton oracle and a separately parameterized mode-preference reward, then ablates the reward while retaining one recurrent PPO trainer. It is a direct design reference for Sam's oracle and reward interfaces.
not_evidence_for: One policy shared across robot morphologies
A fixed MDP across morphology-transfer experiments

mechanisms.name: Closed-loop hybrid-automaton oracle
mechanisms.description: The oracle Xi=(M,X,Lambda,f,S) maps robot/object/target/time feedback to a finite-horizon reference. Continuous reference dynamics operate within a mode; guarded switches change modes.

mechanisms.name: Reach-manipulate-detach abstraction
mechanisms.description: A shared three-mode graph generates coarse robot and object CoM references for soccer and box moving. References are linear interpolations and omit joint targets so joint-space behavior can emerge under simulated dynamics.

mechanisms.name: Oracle-bounded policy exploration
mechanisms.description: PPO optimizes task return while reference-error terminations restrict visited robot/object states to configured permissible bounds around the oracle trajectory during training.

mechanisms.name: History-dependent mode preference reward
mechanisms.description: The reward is -1 whenever the current mode rank is below the maximum rank previously reached in the episode and 0 otherwise; the experiment weights the indicator by -5.0.

mechanisms.name: Softly penalized backward transitions
mechanisms.description: Backward recovery edges remain legal instead of being deleted. A regression is penalized for its lower-rank dwell time, encouraging return to the best rank already reached while preserving perturbation recovery.

mechanisms.name: Single recurrent multi-mode policy
mechanisms.description: One recurrent actor-critic learns all modes and transition maneuvers, outputs actuator PD targets, and observes proprioception, object/target-relative positions, and reference phase.

mechanisms.name: Oracle-free inference
mechanisms.description: After training, policies run without the oracle and with reference-based terminations deactivated; the oracle is a training guide rather than a deployed high-level controller.

mechanisms.name: Recipe-level morphology transfer
mechanisms.description: The same three-mode oracle class and reported reward definition/weights are reused across HECTOR v1, Berkeley Humanoid, G1, and H1, but separate policies are trained and morphology-specific oracle/environment parameters change.

failure_modes.name: Undesirable transition loop
failure_modes.description: Without preference, a policy can kick the ball away, regress from manipulate to reach, chase it, and repeat instead of completing the intended sequence.

failure_modes.name: Fragile inter-policy transitions
failure_modes.description: Three independently trained mode policies fail to hand off robustly; even after later-mode initialization randomization, the baseline falls in 69% of evaluated episodes.

failure_modes.name: Unassigned soccer guard region
failure_modes.description: The released soccer guards assign no destination when the ball is farther than the reach threshold while the robot is within the target threshold; the current mode therefore persists.

failure_modes.name: Simulation-only loco-manipulation evidence
failure_modes.description: The reported soccer and box results are simulation experiments; sim-to-real is stated as ongoing work.

failure_modes.name: Narrow quantitative evaluation
failure_modes.description: The main comparison uses 100 episodes on one soccer-kick setup and reports no confidence intervals, seed dispersion, or significance tests.

failure_modes.name: Partial task-by-robot coverage
failure_modes.description: HECTOR is evaluated on soccer-stop and move-box without regularization; Berkeley, G1, and H1 are evaluated on soccer-kick and move-box with regularization. The study is not a full matched cross-morphology grid.

failure_modes.name: Recipe transfer is not fixed-MDP evidence
failure_modes.description: Separate policies are trained, and released variants change oracle speed, nominal height, episode length, distances, and object dimensions; this does not isolate morphology under Sam's fixed-MDP contract.

failure_modes.name: Unpinned defaults and normalization
failure_modes.description: The paper delegates remaining PPO hyperparameters to Isaac Lab defaults without an exact version and does not report the normalizing constants used inside reward norms.

failure_modes.name: Rank-change typo
failure_modes.description: Sec. IV-C calls manipulate-to-reach a 2-to-1 change even though the stated mapping is reach 0, manipulate 1, detach 2; the equation and mapping indicate 1-to-0.

failure_modes.name: No oracle/reward search
failure_modes.description: Humans author modes, guards, ranks, references, and reward weights; no outer-loop agent proposes or optimizes either design knob.

evaluation.name: Single-policy preference ablation
evaluation.description: Adding preference changes reported soccer-kick success from 28% to 98%, contacts from 5.11 to 9.76, and leaves falls at 0% over 100 episodes.

evaluation.name: Mode-transition distribution
evaluation.description: Preference shifts reach-to-manipulate probability from 0.022 to 0.036 and manipulate-to-reach from 0.021 to 0.001 in the reported soccer-stop analysis.

evaluation.name: Single-policy versus multi-policy baseline
evaluation.description: The single preferenced policy reaches 98% success and 0% falls versus 26% success and 69% falls for three separately trained mode policies switched by the oracle FSM.

evaluation.name: Cross-morphology task synthesis
evaluation.description: Separate policies exhibit different contact strategies on HECTOR v1, Berkeley Humanoid, G1, and H1 while reusing the oracle abstraction and reported reward recipe.

evaluation.name: Oracle-free inference boundary
evaluation.description: Evaluation policies run independently of the oracle with reference-based terminations disabled, testing the learned policy rather than an online FSM-controller composition.

evidence.locator: Metadata and submission history: v3, 8 October 2025
evidence.claim: The latest verified arXiv source is v3; it has the final title and four listed authors.
The oracle supplies finite-horizon references and OGMP restricts policy trajectories to a rho-neighborhood during training.
The oracle is formalized as a hybrid automaton; environment-policy coupling changes mode-transition probabilities and can create undesirable loops.
The tasks use reach, manipulate, and detach modes; feedback contains robot/object/target positions and time; the one-second CoM references are linear interpolations.
The paper reports the exact task and regularization reward expressions and weights, including preference weight -5.0.

evidence.locator: Section IV-C, preference equation and Training details
evidence.claim: The rank-history penalty preserves backward transitions for recovery; training uses recurrent PPO, phase observations, reported state bounds, and a soccer drag model.

evidence.locator: Table I and Section V opening
evidence.claim: Task and robot coverage is partial, and HECTOR is unregularized while Berkeley Humanoid, G1, and H1 are regularized.
Over 100 soccer-kick episodes, the reported success/contact/fall values are 26/12.46/69, 28/5.11/0, and 98/9.76/0 for the three compared policies.
Preference changes reach-to-manipulate and manipulate-to-reach transition probabilities and suppresses the exploitative loop.
The single policy outperforms three separately trained policies, whose handoffs are fragile, while using 0.3 times their learnable parameters.

evidence.locator: Section V opening and Section VI
evidence.claim: Inference deactivates the oracle/reference terminations; validation is in simulation and sim-to-real is future work.
The official project identifies the IROS 2025 paper, code, video, pages, and DOI.
The released soccer oracle uses explicit distance regions and assignments for reach, manipulate, and detach transitions.
The released soccer configuration pins reward weights, 0.4 m guards, termination bounds, and recurrent-policy architecture.
Berkeley, G1, and H1 variants change episode length, start/target distances, oracle speed, and nominal height.
The released preference implementation penalizes every step whose current mode is below the maximum mode reached in the episode.
The released flat-box task sets reach threshold to the box half-diagonal plus 0.05 m.
